Company: Achievers Early College Prep Charter School (AECP)
Company Does: New Jersey's first public charter school for grades 6-12, offering four STEAM pathways (Health Sciences, Digital Media, Audio Engineering, Cisco Computer Networking) where students can earn up to 60 college credits and NOCTI credentials at no cost.
Stage: Growth-stage single-site charter; 543 students and 27.5 FTE teachers (NCES 2024-25), grade span still building out from 6-11 to 6-12; annual revenue $1M-$5M (Exa company record); 23 roles open on its ATS today including a Chief Operations Officer
Why This Company (signal): AECP is a growth-stage NJ charter school (543 students, expanding 6-11 toward a full 6-12 span) whose live Chief Operations Officer posting buries 'technology' as one bullet among facilities, food services, maintenance and security under a single ops/finance hire reporting to the Executive Director -- literal public evidence of Kenneth's target situation, a school with outsourced IT and no technology leadership or board-level technology oversight.
Title: Co-founder and Executive Director of Achievers Early College Prep Charter School
Talk Track:
I'm a fractional CTO for charter and independent school boards that can't answer technology-risk questions -- cybersecurity, AI tools, vendor accountability -- and I work alongside the IT vendors a school already has rather than replacing them. Your open Chief Operations Officer role describes the job as "Oversee network and school operations, including facilities, financial management, technology, food services, maintenance, security, and daily school systems for each of our sites." Technology sits in that sentence between financial management and food services, which means at Achievers it isn't a role, it's a leftover -- whoever you hire inherits it on top of six other departments. The same posting asks that person to "monitor student enrollment, retention, and attendance systems to maximize funding," so your technology systems and your per-pupil funding are the same system; a vendor breach here is an enrollment event, not an IT ticket. Worth naming plainly: you're preparing students for CCNA and CCNP certifications while your own network has no owner on the org chart. Is technology on your board's agenda, or waiting on the COO hire?

-- Kenneth Thomas

Company: Hebrew Public: Charter Schools for Global Citizens
Company Does: Nonprofit charter management organization running a network of secular public charter schools that teach Modern Hebrew, in Brooklyn, Staten Island and Philadelphia, plus affiliate schools in CA, DC, NJ and MN.
Stage: Growth-stage nonprofit CMO — 10 schools and ~4,000 students with 2 more schools 'in the works'; ~45 network staff; founded 2009
Why This Company (signal): Hebrew Public's live Operations Associate posting (HLA, Brooklyn, $50-60k, explicitly 'ideal for someone early in their career') assigns IT-vendor liaison and tech-inventory duties to an entry-level front-office role, and the Philadelphia twin of that role owns 'secure collection, transfer, and storage of sensitive student records' — a 10-school, ~4,000-student charter network whose 45-person network team lists a CEO, CFO, three other chiefs and a Director of Data & Analytics but no technology leader at all, which is exactly the outsourced-IT-with-no-oversight situation Kenneth Thomas sells governance into.
Live Job Title: Operations Associate (HLA, 2186 Mill Avenue, Brooklyn NY)
Title: President & Chief Executive Officer
Talk Track: I do technology governance for charter and independent school networks — the board-facing layer that sits above whichever IT vendor a school already uses, and never replaces them. Your live Operations Associate posting for HLA lists, among the duties of a $50,000-$60,000 role it describes as ideal for someone early in their career: "Assists with technology (e.g. liaising with our IT vendor, navigating mandatory systems, check-out and return of materials, tracking student and staff tech inventory, etc.)." The Philadelphia version of the same role owns "secure collection, transfer, and storage of sensitive student records." Read together, those lines say the person overseeing your IT vendor and holding student data is the newest person in the building — that's a governance gap, not a hiring one. It's also the difference I've watched decide whether a vendor breach costs a school days of parent communication or weeks. Could your board name your IT vendors today?
